params.q: What is the GST rate on restaurant food in India?

search_parameters.q: What is the GST rate on restaurant food in India?

text_blocks.snippet: In India, the GST rate on restaurant food generally falls into two main categories depending on the location and the tariff of the premises:
snippet_highlighted_words: generally falls into two main categories depending on the location and the tariff of the premises

list.snippet: 5% GST (Without Input Tax Credit - ITC): Applicable to standalone restaurants, fast-food joints, cafes, cloud kitchens, and restaurants located inside hotels where the declared room tariff is less than or equal to $7,500 per night. This 5% is typically split as 2.5% CGST and 2.5% SGST (or IGST for interstate supplies). Under this rate, businesses cannot claim Input Tax Credit on their supplies or rent.

18% GST (With Input Tax Credit - ITC): Applicable to restaurants situated inside "specified premises"—which refers to hotels, commercial complexes, or clubs where the declared room tariff for accommodation is above $7,500 per night. Restaurants charging this rate are eligible to claim Input Tax Credit.

Food Delivery Aggregators: If you order via food delivery platforms like Swiggy or Zomato, a 5% GST is collected directly by the platform on the food bill, while delivery fees or platform commissions typically attract an 18% GST.

response.reconstructed_markdown:
In India, the GST rate on restaurant food generally falls into two main categories depending on the location and the tariff of the premises: [0]

- 5% GST \(Without Input Tax Credit \- ITC\): Applicable to standalone restaurants, fast\-food joints, cafes, cloud kitchens, and restaurants located inside hotels where the declared room tariff is less than or equal to $7,500 per night. This 5% is typically split as 2.5% CGST and 2.5% SGST \(or IGST for interstate supplies\). Under this rate, businesses cannot claim Input Tax Credit on their supplies or rent. [0] [1]
- 18% GST \(With Input Tax Credit \- ITC\): Applicable to restaurants situated inside "specified premises"—which refers to hotels, commercial complexes, or clubs where the declared room tariff for accommodation is above $7,500 per night. Restaurants charging this rate are eligible to claim Input Tax Credit. [0] [1]
- Food Delivery Aggregators: If you order via food delivery platforms like [Swiggy](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVqfwsrMqCDEzAKgGzCEQlLTbCWHnTn55lARdfbtbM32xOhr_qjHluSMwlCa5BBt0zA2bETdh1UuKt7qTSW5tTL1K3YthUoMmYMAptlg) or [Zomato](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVJOw8qVW-vLnhj_xgTRf69W11IIaRhS1d1hL4eIC7IezSx4eDyo8MPLBisVRPNPsHJHCYQzgghyR3iA66p78SqRh4j1z-bxOkYf25Ww), a 5% GST is collected directly by the platform on the food bill, while delivery fees or platform commissions typically attract an 18% GST. [1] [2]
